caption:
SpaceX's Falcon 9 has now launched over 300 times, and up-close footage of it climbing still makes people question whether the video is real.

What you're watching is the rocket burning through roughly 660 liters of fuel per second, accelerating from a standstill to over 1,600 km/h inside two minutes. The two Merlin engines produce more thrust than 20 commercial jet engines running at full power, all to push a vehicle that weighs about 550 tonnes off the ground.

Before SpaceX, a single launch like this cost governments around $150 million and the rocket was thrown away after. SpaceX lands the booster and reuses it, which is why they can do this over and over again.
